usage:after-vs-later-sequence.title: after 不能直接替代 later 承接后续动作
usage:after-vs-later-sequence.explanation: 表达“后来……”时，after 不能直接替代 later/then/afterward 来承接后续动作；自然说法是 but later settled 或 but then settled。
usage:after-vs-later-sequence.source: 表达“后来……”时，after 不能直接替代 later/then/afterward 来承接后续动作；自然说法是 but later settled 或 but then settled。

usage:cannot-vs-cant.title: cannot 与 can't 的语域差异
usage:cannot-vs-cant.explanation: cannot 更正式，书面语与强调句中常用；can't 是口语缩略，日常对话更自然。
usage:cannot-vs-cant.source: I cannot stand the smell of smoke.
usage:cannot-vs-cant.example: I cannot (can't) stand waiting in line.

usage:go-for-it-vs-go-ahead.title: go for it 与 go ahead 的语气差异
usage:go-for-it-vs-go-ahead.explanation: go for it 是口语打气语，带朋友间的温度与鼓励，偏“加油、去争取”；go ahead 更像“批准/允许”，回答别人请示时用，意思是“可以，去吧”。正式书面场合一般不用 go for it。
usage:go-for-it-vs-go-ahead.example: A: I'm nervous about the audition. B: Don't be — go for it!

usage:may-proceed-traffic-permission.title: 交通语境中的 may proceed
usage:may-proceed-traffic-permission.explanation: 说明交通信号给予通行许可时，may proceed 比 can continue on 更精确，并隐含确认道路安全后再通行。
usage:may-proceed-traffic-permission.source: A green light on a traffic signal means your car can continue on
usage:may-proceed-traffic-permission.example: When the light turns green, you may proceed if the intersection is clear.

usage:pit-stop-informal-register.title: make a pit stop 为口语非正式表达
usage:pit-stop-informal-register.explanation: 语气轻松、偏口语，适合朋友、家人或熟悉同事之间；较正式的场合可改说 take a short break 或 stop briefly。
usage:pit-stop-informal-register.source: Do you think we can make a pit stop?
usage:pit-stop-informal-register.example: 正式场合：We may take a short break.（口语：Can we make a pit stop?）

usage:pretty-as-adverb-informal.title: pretty as an informal intensifier
usage:pretty-as-adverb-informal.explanation: Here pretty is not the adjective 'beautiful'; it functions as an informal adverb meaning fairly, quite or rather, softening the degree: pretty laid back = fairly relaxed, not extremely relaxed. Common in spoken American English; in formal writing use fairly, quite or rather instead. Common collocations: pretty good, pretty much, pretty sure, pretty busy.
usage:pretty-as-adverb-informal.source: a pretty big price to pay
usage:pretty-as-adverb-informal.example: The movie was pretty good, but the ending was disappointing.

usage:reassure-prepared-tone.title: 用 got ... covered 表达安抚、宽慰语气
usage:reassure-prepared-tone.explanation: 该表达带宽慰语气，强调「已安排妥当、可放心」。常用于团队分工、活动筹备等非正式场合；正式书面可用 has been taken care of / has been handled 替代。
usage:reassure-prepared-tone.example: Relax, the whole itinerary is covered. 放心，整个行程都安排好了。

usage:shall-we-suggestion-friendly.title: Shall we...?：友好地提出建议
usage:shall-we-suggestion-friendly.explanation: Shall we...? 常用于邀请对方一起做某事，语气礼貌、轻松，尤其适合共同活动。它比 Do you want to...? 稍微更优雅一点。
usage:shall-we-suggestion-friendly.source: Shall we take the boat out?
usage:shall-we-suggestion-friendly.example: Shall we sit outside for lunch?

usage:slightly-somewhat-formal-degree.title: slightly / somewhat：略微（正式书面）
usage:slightly-somewhat-formal-degree.explanation: slightly 和 somewhat 是较正式的书面程度副词，表“略微、有点”，正式写作中优先于口语的 a little bit / a bit。

usage:subsequently-formal-transition.title: subsequently 是正式书面的顺序副词
usage:subsequently-formal-transition.explanation: subsequently 表示“随后”，语域偏正式书面（报告、法律、学术），常置句首并以逗号隔开；日常口语用 later、then、afterwards。
usage:subsequently-formal-transition.source: Subsequently, the company opened two new branches.
usage:subsequently-formal-transition.example: Subsequently, the company opened two new branches.
